title: NEB Class 12 Mathematics — Linear Programming — 2024
subject: mathematics
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Maximise Z = 40x + 50y subject to 2x + y ≤ 20, x + 2y ≤ 20, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0. Solve graphically.
questions.solution:
**Feasible region:** bounded by the axes and the two constraint lines.

Corner points from the intersections:
- (0, 0) → Z = 0
- (10, 0) → Z = 400
- (0, 10) → Z = 500
- intersection of 2x + y = 20 and x + 2y = 20: solving gives x = y = **20/3 ≈ 6.67** → Z = 40(20/3) + 50(20/3) = 600.

By the corner-point theorem the optimum is at a vertex: **maximum Z = 600 at x = y = 20/3**.

(Checking the interior point confirms the value is below 600, and the region is bounded, so the maximum exists.)
questions.knowledgeNote: Evaluate Z at EVERY corner: the optimum is always at a vertex for a linear objective on a convex feasible region.

questions.question: Define feasible region, optimal solution and corner-point theorem in linear programming.
questions.solution:
**Feasible region:** the common region satisfying all the constraints (including non-negativity) of a linear programming problem — it is a convex polygon.

**Optimal solution:** the feasible point (set of values of the decision variables) at which the objective function attains its maximum or minimum value.

**Corner-point theorem (fundamental theorem of LPP):** if the feasible region is bounded, the objective function attains its optimum at a corner (vertex) of the feasible region; if two adjacent vertices give the same optimum, every point on the segment joining them is optimal.
questions.knowledgeNote: This is why the graphical method evaluates only vertices — it is a theorem, not a shortcut, and the examiner expects it stated.

questions.question: A factory makes two products A and B. A needs 2 hours of machine time and 1 hour of labour; B needs 1 hour of machine time and 3 hours of labour. The factory has 40 machine hours and 60 labour hours per day. If the profit is Rs 30 on A and Rs 40 on B, formulate the LPP to maximise the profit.
questions.solution:
Let x = units of A and y = units of B produced per day.

**Objective:** maximise Z = 30x + 40y (profit in rupees).

**Constraints:**
- machine time: 2x + y ≤ 40
- labour time: x + 3y ≤ 60
- non-negativity: x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.

The solution is obtained by plotting the two lines, finding the feasible region and evaluating Z at its corner points (one of which is the intersection x = 12, y = 16 giving Z = 1000).
questions.knowledgeNote: Always define the variables and write the non-negativity restrictions explicitly — they are part of the formulation and carry marks.
